title: Unified spatiotemporal quantum states and spatiotemporal entanglement from Kirkwood-Dirac phase space
abstract: The notion of a spatiotemporal quantum state extends the conventional concept of a spatial quantum state to the spatiotemporal domain. Such states are represented by unit-trace operators that encode correlations among quantum events distributed across space and time. In this work, we use the spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac phase space to provide a unified characterization of spatiotemporal quantum states. Spatiotemporal states obtained from Kirkwood-Dirac distributions are generally non-Hermitian and nonnormal; whereas those constructed from Margenau-Hill distributions are Hermitian. We provide a unification via (quasi)probabilistic mixture of Kirkwwod-Dirac spatiotemporal states which encompasses almost all existing formulations of spatiotemporal quantum states. We derive recursive expressions for spatiotemporal states and elucidate the relation between Kirkwood-Dirac nonclassicality and the temporality of spatiotemporal states. We further extend the construction to many-fold correlation functions and establish its connection with out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). We also develop a more general unifying framework based on (quasi)probabilistic mixture of $s$-parametrized spatiotemporal states and establish their Petz time reversal and application in studying Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) condition in two-time setting. Finally, we apply this framework to characterize quantum entanglement in spacetime and analyze spatiotemporal entanglement using several complementary entropy measures.
summary: This paper introduces the spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac phase space as a comprehensive mathematical framework to unify the description of quantum states that depend on both space and time. It develops methods to quantify spatiotemporal entanglement and relates these concepts to advanced tools like Out-of-Time-Ordered Correlators and the Kubo-Martin-Schwinger condition. It is a highly theoretical contribution to quantum information in spacetime.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a unified mathematical framework for characterizing spatiotemporal quantum states and quantifying spatiotemporal entanglement.
main_result: It establishes the spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac phase space as a unifying structure that encompasses various existing state formalisms and connects them to concepts like OTOCs and KMS conditions.
method: The authors utilize generalized probabilistic theories (GPTs) based on the spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distribution, deriving recursive relations and employing techniques like Petz time reversal and entropy measures.
model_or_system: The focus is on abstract quantum systems described by spatiotemporal quantum states ($\Upsilon$), extending concepts from standard quantum mechanics to include correlations across space and time.
key_observables: Spatiotemporal entanglement, various entropy measures (e.g., Spectral, Mutual), and the characterization of nonclassicality via Kirkwood-Dirac distributions.
important_parameters: The parameter $s$ used in $s$-parametrized spatiotemporal states, and the time separation in two-time correlation functions.
main_assumptions: The framework is primarily developed for finite-dimensional systems, although the general structure is proposed for broader applications.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the equivalence between the spatiotemporal quantum state, the information-complete Kirkwood-Dirac distribution, and Wightman correlation functions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the spatiotemporal state using the Kirkwood-Dirac phase space, unifying different state constructions (KD vs. MH), extending the formalism to many-fold correlations and OTOCs, and finally applying the framework to characterize entanglement and study thermal equilibrium via the KMS condition.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly abstract and general mathematical toolset for analyzing quantum correlations in time, which is crucial for understanding quantum field theory dynamics and non-equilibrium quantum many-body physics.
